stemBlocks.value: A trader bought 500 oranges for $2 000. 50 oranges were spoiled and the rest were sold at $6 each. (a) Calculate the total revenue. (b) Calculate the percentage profit or loss.
Think first: Only the oranges actually sold bring in money, but all 500 were paid for.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p020-q18 from workbook page 20.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the number of oranges actually sold.
Multiply by the price per orange to get the revenue.
Express the profit as a percentage of the cost price.

strategyBlocks.value: Find how many oranges were sold, multiply by the selling price for the revenue, compare with the $2 000 cost, then express the difference as a percentage of the cost.

whyThisWorks.value: Spoiled stock is a real cost: the trader paid for all 500 oranges but earned from only 450, so the effective cost per orange sold rises from $4.00 to about $4.44. Percentage profit still uses the full $2 000 outlay as its base because that is the money actually risked. This is why wastage eats into a margin so quickly.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying 500 by $6 and ignoring the spoiled oranges.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying 500 by $6 and ignoring the spoiled oranges.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the cost of only the 450 sold oranges as the base.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using the cost of only the 450 sold oranges as the base.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing the profit by the revenue instead of the cost.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing the profit by the revenue instead of the cost.

examTip.value: Read any sentence about wastage twice, then write two separate numbers: how many were bought and how many were sold.
